newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa labour wants rich to pay more in budget.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa labour wants rich to pay more in budget.

text.p: The South African government should raise taxes on the rich and and corporations to help fund job-creating investment and address severe inequalities, the largest labour federation said on Tuesday.
In a briefing note issued ahead of Wednesday's 1997/98 budget, the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) called for:
- the introduction of a capital gains tax;
- a 55 percent tax rate on the "super rich" (the current top rate of tax is 45 percent);
- taxation of luxury goods at a higher rate of Value Added Tax (VAT);
- increased levels of corporate tax following systematic reductions in recent years;
- the closure of tax avoidance loopholes used by the wealthy;
- a three-year levy on company profits of, say, five percent to finance housing and public works;
- and increased spending on housing, healthcare and education.

Cosatu general secretary Sam Shilowa also said the union movement opposed the removal of exchange controls which would allow domestic holders of wealth to move it offshore, beyond the reach of government.

Most analysts expect Finance Minister Trevor Manuel to announce few tax changes in a conservative budget designed to sell South Africa to global investors. There is speculation that he will use the occasion to announce the next steps in the phased relxation of capital controls.
